# pacchettino: file-based job queue for D

pacchettino is a job queue for the D programming language made of plain directories on disk. Producers add jobs (some bytes, or a file), consumers in other processes or threads process them. Jobs are on disk before `send*` returns, each job goes to one consumer only, and jobs left half done by a crashed process are detected. No server, no database, no dependencies. Linux, macOS, BSD and Windows. MIT license.

- Full reference: https://trikko.github.io/pacchettino/llms-full.txt
- Rules for agents: https://trikko.github.io/pacchettino/AGENTS.md (as a skill: https://trikko.github.io/pacchettino/SKILL.md)
- API documentation: https://trikko.github.io/pacchettino/
- Source: https://github.com/trikko/pacchettino

## Core Concepts

- **Pacchettino**: `new Pacchettino(dir, keepPolicy = KeepPolicy.ALL)`. Every producer and consumer opens the same directory; it creates `scheduled/`, `queued/`, `processing/`, `success/`, `failed/`, `interrupted/`, `tmp/`.
- **Sending**: `sendData(string or ubyte[], delay = Duration.zero)`, `sendFile(path, copyFile = true, delay = Duration.zero)`. Both return the job id, a UUIDv7 string.
- **Receiving**: set `onDataReceived = (id, ubyte[] data) => Result` and `onFileReceived = (id, name, path) => Result`, then call `receiveOne(timeout)` in a loop (or `receiveOne()`, `receive()`). Callbacks run in the calling thread; the defaults return `FAILED`.
- **Result**: `SUCCESS`, `FAILED` (both final), `RETRY` (queued again, after `retryDelay` if set). An exception from the callback is `FAILED`.
- **Order**: random by default, FIFO with `randomize = false`.
- **Crash recovery**: jobs of a dead consumer are moved to `interrupted/` by the next `receive*`; `requeueAll()` tries them again.
- **Status**: `status(id)` → `Status.SCHEDULED/QUEUED/PROCESSING/SUCCESS/FAILED/INTERRUPTED/UNKNOWN`; `sentAt(id)`; `is*` and `count*` methods.
- **crashDetection**: `PID` (default) or `LOCK_FILE`, needed when consumers run in different containers on the same directory.
- **durable**: `queue.durable = true` flushes every write to the disk (fsync), so jobs survive power cuts too; much slower.
- **KeepPolicy**: `NONE`, `SUCCESS`, `FAILED`, `INTERRUPTED`, `ALL` (combine with `|`): which processed jobs stay on disk. `cleanup(which, olderThan)` removes them.

## Installation & Basic Usage

`dub add pacchettino`. dmd or ldc2.

```d
import pacchettino;
import core.time;

// Producer
auto queue = new Pacchettino("/var/spool/myapp");
queue.sendFile("/tmp/video.mp4");
queue.sendData("remind 42", 10.minutes);

// Consumer (another program)
auto queue = new Pacchettino("/var/spool/myapp");
queue.onFileReceived = (string id, string name, string path) {
    upload(path);
    return Pacchettino.Result.SUCCESS;
};
queue.onDataReceived = (string id, ubyte[] data) => Pacchettino.Result.SUCCESS;

while (true)
    queue.receiveOne(5.seconds);
```

## Limits

One machine only (crash detection uses local PIDs or lock files: no NFS or shared folders). No priorities, no attempt limit, no notifications (consumers poll). File names up to 200 bytes.
